name: Pharaoh
description: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Pharaoh's army comes out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans besieging Jerusalem hear of it, they depart from the city.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: Pharaoh's army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land: So all of a sudden, this is the example. This is King Zedekiah who went to inquire to Jeremiah concerning what the Lord can do for them to stop this army that's coming to destroy them, the Chaldeans of Babylon. And guess what he did? The Lord say, No, don't come counsel with me now, because you already ask Egypt for help. That's a lot of us today. You went to go vote. You upholding this system. You partake in politics. You partake in the holidays. Now all of a sudden when tragedy strike, you looking for help from God. God said, nuh-uh, go back to your strength.
The word of the Most High comes to Jeremiah for the king of Judah: Pharaoh's army that came to help shall return to Egypt into their own land.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: The word of the Most High came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes to take great stones and hide them in the clay of the brick kiln at the entry of Pharaoh's house, in the sight of the men of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: In chapter 46 Nebuchadnezzar wipes out Egypt, and then Jeremiah goes back to before that Pharaoh smote Gaza: Philistine is the ancient name for Palestine, and this Pharaoh goes into Esau as in Romans 9 and Revelation 11.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

points: Pharaoh smote Gaza, and today Amalek smites Gaza. The Philistines are the Palestinians, and the prophecy falls on both.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

points: Now he is going against another country: “against the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.” Remember the Philistines are the Africans. You have remnants of Israel in Africa, scattered all throughout, but then you actually have the Africans that are not our people.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: In the tenth year, tenth month, twelfth day, the word came to set Ezekiel's face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, the great dragon that lies in the midst of his rivers and says, My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.

note.label: Ezekiel 29: The Judgment Against Pharaoh and Egypt

points: In the eleventh year the word came that the Most High has broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and it shall not be bound up to be healed or made strong to hold the sword.
He will break both Pharaoh's arms, strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put His sword in his hand, scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and they shall know that He is the Lord.

“Son of man, speak unto Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his multitude”: his army, his realm. “Whom art thou like in thy greatness?” Who do you resemble, Pharaoh, in your greatness, before you fall? This chapter is a parable, a comparison between Pharaoh in his greatness and someone else.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End

points: “To whom art thou thus like in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden?” He asks the question again. Pharaoh, before Assyria conquered you, you were like Adam: boastful, people came under you for sanctuary, you had resources, wealth, power, everybody came to you to learn wisdom. Now where are you? Assyria came and destroyed you. Adam was like both of them in a certain way: like Assyria in his glory and like Pharaoh in glory, but both their falls were terrible and everybody felt it, the same way everyone felt it when Adam fell.

“Yet shalt thou be brought down with the trees of Eden unto the nether parts of the earth”, with everybody else. “This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, saith the Lord God”: but it’s not just Pharaoh, it’s who he’s compared to also. Pharaoh and Adam.

note.label: Good And Evil | Generation To Generation: From Beginning To End
